title: Etaleness along a closed subscheme from its infinitesimal neighbourhoods
statement: Let $g:X\to S$ be a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] between locally Noetherian schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $Z\subseteq S$ be a closed subscheme with quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal J$, let $Z_n\subseteq S$ be its $n$-th infinitesimal neighbourhood, the closed subscheme cut out by $\mathcal J^{n+1}$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], and $X_n=Z_n\times_SX$ [def-pc-base-change]. If $X_n\to Z_n$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] for every $n\ge0$, then $g$ is etale at every point of $g^{-1}(Z)$: there is an open subscheme $W\subseteq X$ containing $g^{-1}(Z)$ such that $g|_W:W\to S$ is etale.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 0A43 (label lemma-check-smoothness-on-infinitesimal-nbhds), part (2), with its proof via Lemma lemma-lifting-along-artinian-at-point (Artinian infinitesimal lifting criterion at a point); etale at a point as in Morphisms, Definition 02GI

proof.text: Fix $x\in g^{-1}(Z)$ and put $s=g(x)$. By etale locality on source and target [lem-weil-pbc-etale-locality] we may replace $S$ by an affine neighbourhood of $s$ and $X$ by an affine neighbourhood of $x$. Passing to the local rings at these points gives the finite-type local homomorphism $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}\to B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$; Noetherianity follows from [pqf-def-locnoeth].

source.place: Lemma 0A43, proof of (2), localization at a point

proof.text: Let $I=\mathcal J_s\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$. The stalk of the $(n+1)$-fold ideal product is the product of the stalks, so $(\mathcal J^{n+1})_s=I^{n+1}$; pulling the ideal back along $A\to B$ gives $I^{n+1}B$. Hence the pullbacks of $Z_n$ and $X_n=Z_n\times_SX$ to the chosen local schemes are respectively $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^{n+1})$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(B/I^{n+1}B)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-locality], etaleness of $X_n\to Z_n$ at $x$ is exactly etaleness of this local ring map at $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak m_B$ (the point induced by $x$). Thus every quotient map in the criterion is etale at $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Lemma 0A43, proof of (2), identification of infinitesimal neighbourhoods after localization

proof.text: Apply the Artinian infinitesimal criterion for etaleness at a point to the local map $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$; it follows that $g$ is etale at $x$.

By the finite-type locally Noetherian etale-locus openness node [lem-weil-pbc-etale-locus-open] (Stacks 0476 and 0A43), the etale locus of $g$ is open. Taking it as $W$ (or the union of its neighbourhoods) gives an open subscheme containing $g^{-1}(Z)$, and $g|_W$ is etale.

source.place: Lemma 0A43, conclusion of part (2); etale locus openness
